sections.content:
35,605 people

were counted on the census as "school secretaries" in England and Wales in March 2021.
School secretaries provide administrative support in schools by keeping and maintaining school records and performing a range of routine clerical tasks within the school.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "school secretaries" there were more women than men (96.5% compared with 3.5%).

This means "school secretaries" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "secretarial and related occupations".

Men made up 3.5% and women made up 96.5% of "school secretaries"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "school secretaries" included:

  • speech and language therapists
  • early education and childcare services managers
  • veterinary nurses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "school secretaries" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "school secretaries", 19.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "school secretaries" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "school secretaries" included:

  • printers
  • inspectors of standards and regulations
  • librarians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "school secretaries" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of women than men with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "school secretaries" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "school secretaries", 9.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (53.8% compared with 46.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (99.1%) than self-employed (0.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
